# Fighter Side-Branch Summary Generated by the Water-Aircraft Audit — V18

This file exists to prevent later contradiction; it does not replace the full fixed-wing canon.

## A6M

- Do not assume Kinsei conversion automatically.
- Strong Sakae A6M remains useful.
- Kinsei 54 long-wing bridge is a serious candidate around 584–590 km/h / ~2.9 t, retaining carrier-like wing loading.
- Kinsei 62 is more a successor-delay insurance branch than the automatic main line.
- Future Reppu family must remain in the comparison; do not over-invest in extreme A6M re-engining.

## J2M

- Existing past mechanism is preserved: extension-shaft torsion, cooling fan/cowl, oil cooling and prop/governor must be qualified independently.
- Worldline measurement/rotating-machinery knowledge shortens diagnosis; it does not erase the mechanisms.
- J2M2 1942 Q3 technical shadow around 600–605 km/h, 6 km ~5:10–5:30.
- dedicated high-altitude turbo J2M is more technically credible than history, but requirement/production remains history-gated.

## N1K1-J

- CRP comparison remains valid because Kyofu CRP succeeds.
- geometry audit shows CRP does not remove the mid-wing long-gear problem; prop radius reduction is too small.
- a CRP N1K1-J can work technically and still lose the production trade to a normal 4-blade.
- worldline N1K1-J is better described as a powerful but structurally/maintenance-expensive bridge than a simple defective fighter.

## N1K2-J

Dedicated technical closeout candidate:

- 3.82–3.92 t normal combat weight.
- 602–606 km/h, center ~604.
- 6 km ~5:50–6:10.
- 20 mm x4, roughly 800–900 rounds total working band.
- automatic combat flap credible for this generation if prior Kyofu/manual-map path is funded.

Procurement remains open because A6M/Kinsei bridge, J2M, Reppu and production/engine allocation all matter.
